lessons.title: Library Orientation Changes
lessons.learningObjective: Track locations and a revised opening time during a campus library orientation.

lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “opposite the lifts” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “rather than” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “booked online” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “at least fifteen minutes” only with the meaning stated here.

activities.prompt: Which detail changed in the recording?

options.label: The detail stated in sentence three
A detail not mentioned in the recording

answer.text: Group study rooms are on the second floor and must be booked online.

activities.feedback: Use the exact changed detail rather than a plausible topic word.

activities.prompt: Write the second sentence exactly as you hear it.

answer.text: The help desk is now opposite the lifts rather than beside the main doors.

activities.feedback: Check content words, function words and the stated detail.

activities.prompt: Retrieve the fourth sentence without opening the transcript.

answer.text: On Fridays, the building closes at seven instead of nine.

activities.feedback: Opening the answer makes this attempt coaching-only.

activities.prompt: Shadow the final two sentences with thought-group pauses.

answer.text: On Fridays, the building closes at seven instead of nine. Return laptops to the desk at least fifteen minutes before closing.

activities.feedback: Aim for rhythm and intelligibility; this is coaching, not independent evidence.

activities.prompt: Retell the practical outcome in two sentences.

answer.text: Mention the main change and the required action, using opposite the lifts where suitable.

activities.feedback: Retell remains coaching-only without an independent evaluator.

accessibility.label: Library Orientation Changes

lessons.title: Measuring Useful Urban Shade
lessons.learningObjective: Separate evidence about shade location from a distractor about total tree numbers.

lexicalTargets.meaning: a number reported by an authority
lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “official figure” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “heat exposure” only with the meaning stated here.

lexicalTargets.meaning: the spread of branches and leaves
lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “canopy width” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “maintenance priorities” only with the meaning stated here.

activities.prompt: State the passage’s central claim in one sentence.

answer.text: Separate evidence about shade location from a distractor about total tree numbers.

activities.feedback: A strong answer preserves the scope of the passage.

activities.prompt: Which expression best preserves “official figure”?

options.label: a number reported by an authority

answer.text: a number reported by an authority

activities.feedback: Match meaning and claim strength, not just topic.

activities.prompt: Identify a plausible statement that the passage does not establish.

answer.text: A broad universal claim that removes the passage’s stated limitation.

activities.feedback: Distractors often repeat vocabulary while changing scope or causality.

activities.prompt: Find the sentence that limits the main claim and explain its function.

answer.text: The limiting sentence prevents the evidence from supporting a broader conclusion.

activities.feedback: Look for contrast markers and cautious reporting verbs.

activities.prompt: Write 70–90 words using “heat exposure” to evaluate the passage.

answer.text: A complete paragraph should state a claim, cite a passage detail and preserve one limitation.

activities.feedback: This follow-up is coaching-only until independently evaluated.

lessons.title: Cause, Contribution and Result
lessons.learningObjective: Choose paraphrases that preserve the strength of a causal claim.

lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “result in” only with the meaning stated here.

lexicalTargets.meaning: contribute without being the only cause
lexicalTargets.usageNote: Use “play a role in” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “arise from” only with the meaning stated here.
Use “have little effect on” only with the meaning stated here.

activities.prompt: Recall a precise meaning for “result in”.

answer.text: cause a stated outcome

activities.feedback: Keep the strength and grammatical role of the expression.

activities.prompt: Choose the expression matching: contribute without being the only cause.

answer.text: play a role in

activities.feedback: Use the meaning note rather than surface similarity.

activities.prompt: Write one academic sentence using “result in”.

answer.text: The sentence should use the expression in its stated sense and register.

activities.feedback: Check collocation, grammar and claim strength.

activities.prompt: Write 70–90 words using “result in” and “play a role in”.

answer.text: The paragraph should connect both expressions coherently without changing their meanings.

activities.feedback: Prefer a clear claim and one supporting example.

activities.prompt: Paraphrase “arise from” without increasing certainty.

answer.text: begin because of

activities.feedback: Preserve modality and scope.
